do.prompt: Production sprite animation study for an original children's piano-learning game. Use the supplied coral note ONLY as a material, palette and character-family reference. Create ONE clean sprite sheet: exactly 4 equal columns and 3 equal rows, on a genuinely transparent background, with generous transparent gutters. Square sheet, each cell is a tall portrait frame. Each of the 12 cells contains the SAME single CORAL RED DO musical QUARTER NOTE character: a plump slightly tilted oval notehead, one straight rounded stem attached at the RIGHT going UP, NO flag, NO extra music symbols. Hand-molded matte plasticine with fine tactile texture, broad soft upper-left lighting, no metal or neon, no outside glow. Lock body silhouette, head/stem proportions, camera, lighting, coral #ff7b80, scale and exact anchor position across all cells. Full stem and head fit in every frame, no clipping, no feet or hands. Animate the FACE, with only extremely subtle squash within 2 percent; keep musical geometry stable for placement on a real staff. Row 1 neutral/idle frames: attentive open dark eyes, relaxed neutral small mouth; frame2 softly blinks, frame3 opens, frame4 returns exactly to frame1. Row 2 correct-answer joy frames: expression brightens, gentle closed-eye smile, happy open smile with tiny pink tongue, returns to a warm smile; friendly small celebration, no body jumping. Row 3 wrong-answer mild-disappointment frames: surprised small mouth, slightly sad curved eyebrows and tiny frown, reassuring sympathetic expression, returns toward neutral. Never angry, frightening, crying or shaming. Face remains upright despite oval tilt. Use simple dimensional charcoal eye and mouth pieces, tiny pink tongue only when smiling. No text, frame labels, numbers, borders, scenery, floor, staff, clef, shadows outside the object, duplicate notes in one cell or other objects. Clean authentic alpha cutout, consistent evenly spaced grid.
